reason: 5.19.0 fixes two things the approvals card said wrongly. (1) 'Reads only, changes nothing.' travelled in the same warnings array as 'Work other people pushed can be lost.', so the safest action on the queue wore the amber attention colour and a warning triangle - backwards on a surface whose job is to make attention scarce, and against .impeccable.md, which reserves that colour for when attention is actually required. PlainDescription gains a `reassurance` field, populated last in describeAction so describeBash's calm-eligibility filter keeps deciding whether the phrase survives at all; a reassurance suppressed as unsupportable can never be resurrected. (2) bash.sql.drop and bash.sql.delete emit 'This cannot be undone.' as a warning, which is the exact sentence the card renders as its red band, so an irreversible DROP TABLE printed that sentence twice in two different colours. It is now dropped from the warning list only when the classifier actually said reversible:false, so the no-intel path keeps its only signal. Because neither the decision detail page nor the Telegram/Discord cards have a band, both now state irreversibility in words - which also closes a real gap where an `rm -rf` notification never said it at all. Platform only, no Node/Python SDK surface change.
